blocks: Avoid arching away from the backrest or letting the elbows travel far behind the body. Reduce the load or adjust the starting position if the machine pulls the shoulders into an uncomfortable stretch.
Source and video: Mayo Clinic's chest press with a weight machine.
Practice a supported overhead press for the shoulders and triceps on a guided machine.
Adjust the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height. Plant the feet and keep the back against the pad.
Press the handles overhead without forcing the elbows into lockout, then lower them under control to the starting height.

Sets, repetitions, resistance, and rest follow the training plan. Establish a repeatable movement with a light load first; add resistance gradually after completing the planned repetitions with consistent control.

Avoid arching away from the backrest. The machine guides the path, so it asks less coordination than the barbell Exercise/Body/Strength/Overhead Press or Exercise/Body/Strength/Dumbbell Overhead Press; Huberman prefers the free-weight versions for that reason.
Demonstration: Huberman's machine shoulder press, 1:45. Full notes: Person/Andrew Huberman/Book/26/Protocols/YouTube/26/09/Day 7 - Shoulders and Arms.
Practice extending the elbows overhead against a cable to stretch and train the long head of the triceps.
Day 7 at 8:12 in Person/Andrew Huberman/Book/26/Protocols/YouTube/26/09/Day 7 - Shoulders and Arms

Set the cable above and behind you, face away from the stack, and hold the handles behind the head. Step far enough from the machine to feel a stretch on the triceps at the start. Lock the lats and brace the core.

Extend the elbows to press the handles forward and overhead, like a soccer throw-in, then return to the stretched position. The movement is mostly at the elbow; as the set gets harder, let the shoulders come back a little while keeping the stretch.

Huberman usually does three sets to or near failure. Sets, repetitions, resistance, and rest follow the training plan. Establish a repeatable movement with a light load first; add resistance gradually after completing the planned repetitions with consistent control.
